title: PlayStation owners plan a week-long "PSBlackout" protest over over Sony killing discs in 2028
summary: PlayStation owners are organizing a week-long "PSBlackout" protest in response to Sony's plan to end support for physical game discs in 2028. Organizers aim to spotlight concerns about ownership, the used-game market, preservation and access, coordinating actions via social media and gaming communities to pressure Sony and raise public awareness.
content:
PlayStation owners worldwide are planning a week-long "PSBlackout" protest in response to Sony's announcement that it will phase out support for physical game discs in 2028. Organizers say the blackout will be a coordinated pause in PlayStation-related activity intended to draw public attention to the implications of the change.

The protest movement has been promoted through gaming forums, community groups and social platforms. Participants cite concerns about long-term ownership of purchased titles, the future of the used-game market, preservation of gaming history, and access for players who lack reliable high-speed internet. These issues, organizers argue, deserve clearer transition plans and safeguards from major platform holders.

Planned actions associated with the "PSBlackout" include a temporary boycott of new PlayStation purchases during the protest week, reduced engagement on PlayStation Network, and amplification of the hashtag "#PSBlackout" to increase visibility. Details and commitments vary among groups, and coordination is ongoing across different regions and time zones.

Sony's shift away from discs toward digital distribution has been framed by the company as part of a modernization effort that can offer convenience and potential environmental benefits. Critics counter that an all-digital future may raise costs for consumers, reduce resale and sharing options, and hinder preservation of older titles.

Industry analysts say the ultimate impact of the protest will depend on the scale of participation and whether retailers, publishers or regulators respond. Regardless of immediate outcomes, the "PSBlackout" underscores the tensions that can arise as the games industry moves further into digital-only distribution and raises broader questions about ownership, access and consumer rights.
